page: Amazon Web Services i4g.2xlarge is a storage-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 64-bit ARM architecture. The instance provides 8 dedicated physical cores running on AWS Neoverse-N1 (ARMv8) processors clocked at 2.5 GHz with a single thread per core. Memory capacity is 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB per core allocation. For high-throughput local storage, the instance includes an attached 1875 GB NVMe SSD. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 5 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses assigned.

Benchmark results show balanced throughput for database and memory-bound operations, paired with moderate execution speed across pure compute tests. The instance achieves 9.8 million operations per second on Redis SET workloads and registers 5,224.61 on PassMark database operations. In stress-ng, CPU performance measures 1,519.59 in single-core and 12,132.09 in multi-core testing. Synthetic compute benchmarks reflect the characteristics of first-generation Neoverse-N1 cores, recording a Geekbench single-core score of 937.0 and a multi-core score of 5,360.0. Compression benchmarks show lower throughput, including 20.3 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip and 7.19 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3 decompression.

The 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio combined with high-capacity local NVMe storage provides strong resource density for data-intensive workloads without incurring excessive hardware overhead. Workloads demanding high single-thread clock speeds or x86 instruction sets will face limitations, but systems benefiting from local I/O speed, steady multi-core execution, and substantial RAM operate efficiently. The instance fits transactional databases, distributed NoSQL datastores, real-time search engines, in-memory caches, and local analytics pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services i4g.2xlarge is a storage-optimized instance powered by an 8-core AWS Neoverse-N1 ARMv8 processor at 2.5 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. It is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB per physical core, and features a bundled 1875 GB local NVMe SSD along with a 5 Gbps baseline network interface. In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates consistent multi-core and data-handling throughput, reaching 9.8 million Redis SET operations per second and solid PassMark database metrics, though single-threaded compute and compression scores fall in lower percentiles. The pairing of local high-speed NVMe storage with an ample 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio makes the i4g.2xlarge well tailored for low-latency databases, distributed NoSQL stores, caching layers, and search indexing workloads that prioritize direct disk I/O and memory capacity over peak compute frequencies.
